sub_tasks.requirements: Fine-tuning models in the NetHack environment using kickstarting (KS) has been correctly implemented

For NetHack the Kickstarting knowledge retention method is implemented; an auxiliary loss is implemented as $\mathcal{L}_{KS}(\theta) = \mathbb{E}_{s \sim \pi_\mathcal{B}_\theta} \left[ D_{KL} \left( \pi_{*}(s) \parallel \pi_{\theta}(s) \right) \right]$, where $\pi_\star$ is the frozen pre-trained model for NetHack from (Tuyls et al., 2023), $\pi_\theta$ is the current model, and $\mathcal{B}_\theta$ is a buffer of states

verification.spec: Construct a small dummy policy and a frozen 'pretrained' policy, and a batch of states sampled by the online policy. Call the implemented KS loss function and verify: (1) it returns KL(pi_star(s) || pi_theta(s)) averaged over on-policy states; (2) gradient flows to pi_theta but not pi_star (pi_star.requires_grad=False); (3) when pi_theta == pi_star, loss ≈ 0.

sub_tasks.requirements: When fine-tuning models in the NetHack environment using kickstarting (KS), the auxiliary loss is computed on a buffer of data generated by the online policy

verification.spec: Inspect the Kickstarting loss implementation for NetHack: verify that the KL-divergence auxiliary loss L_KS = E_{s~pi_theta}[KL(pi_*(s) || pi_theta(s))] uses states sampled from the current (online) policy's rollout buffer, not from the pre-training/expert dataset. Run one training step and log the source of KS batch states to confirm they come from rollouts.

sub_tasks.requirements: Fine-tuning models in the NetHack environment using behavioural cloning (BC) has been correctly implemented

In the behavioural cloning (BC) implementation for NetHack, before training, a subset of states $\mathcal{S}_{BC}$ is gathered on the 8000 trajectories generated by the AutoAscend algorithm, and a buffer is constructed as $\mathcal{B}_{BC} := \{(s,\pi_\star(s)) : s \in \mathcal{S}_{BC} \}$, i.e., the action that the AutoAscend algorithm took on each of such states is recorded

verification.spec: Run the BC buffer construction for NetHack: load the 8000 AutoAscend trajectories, subsample a set S_BC of states, query pi_* on each, and store (s, pi_*(s)) pairs in B_BC. Verify B_BC is built before training starts (not during) and that during fine-tuning the BC auxiliary loss draws only from this precomputed buffer.

sub_tasks.requirements: In the behavioural cloning (BC) implementation for NetHack, when fine-tuning, an auxiliary loss is implemented as $\mathcal{L}_{BC}(\theta) = \mathbb{E}_{s \sim \mathcal{B}_{BC}} \left[ D_{KL} \left( \pi_{*}(s) \parallel \pi_{\theta}(s) \right) \right]$, where $\pi_\star$ is the frozen pre-trained model from (Tuyls et al., 2023), and $\mathcal{B}_{BC}$ is a buffer of data containing states from the AutoAscend algorithm

verification.spec: Build a small BC buffer B_BC of (state, pi_star(state)) pairs and a dummy pi_theta. Call the implemented BC auxiliary loss and verify: (1) it computes KL(pi_star(s) || pi_theta(s)) averaged over states sampled from B_BC (not online rollouts); (2) sampling is from the fixed buffer; (3) loss = 0 when pi_theta matches pi_star on those states.

sub_tasks.requirements: Fine-tuning models in the NetHack environment using elastic weight consolidation (EWC) has been correctly implemented

For NetHack, the diagonal Fisher matrix can be computed as $F_{ii} = \mathbb{E} [\Delta_\thetal(\theta)_i^2]$, where the expectation is computed using the squared gradients of the loss wrt. each parameter over 10000 batches sampled from the NLD-AA subset of 8000 monk trajectories

verification.spec: Verify the Fisher-computation routine: (1) it iterates over 10000 batches drawn from the NLD-AA monk-trajectory subset (or a documented dataset loader with the same specification); (2) for each parameter it accumulates the mean of squared per-example gradients of the loss; (3) resulting Fisher has same shape as model parameters and is non-negative. Test on a toy model with a known analytic Fisher.

sub_tasks.requirements: For NetHack, the Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC) knowledge retention method is implemented; the auxiliary loss is implemented as $\mathcal{L}_{\text{aux}} (\theta) = \sum_i F^i(\theta_\star^i-\theta^i)^2$, where $\theta$ is the weights of the current model, $\theta_\star$ is the weights of the pre-trained model from (Tuyls et al., 2023), and $F$ is the diagonal of the Fisher matrix

verification.spec: Given a tiny model with known theta_star and diagonal Fisher F, call the implemented EWC auxiliary loss and check it equals sum_i F_i (theta_star_i - theta_i)^2. Verify (1) exact numeric match on a hand-computed example; (2) loss is 0 when theta==theta_star; (3) grad w.r.t. theta equals 2*F*(theta - theta_star).
